scope: All 235 asset items, all recursive human-facing card layers, every deck/bundle member and physical count; no production writes.
reviewMethod: Full human-facing text pass across every asset, including custom-card layer content and token backs.
Compared core and three expansion inventories, card rules and collected FAQ clarifications. The two FAQ review files map all 402 comments.
Read all 13 Homeworld card faces visually. Selected explicit card strengths and Richese threshold over conflicting example/code values, with decisions recorded.
Checked TreacheryCardManager.cs and Map.cs mappings against package multiplicities and territories/sectors.
Kept approved pre-existing Nexus, Stronghold, Leader Skill, Storm and board stock unchanged.

findings.before: Ixian separate stronghold within a sand territory sector. Immune to storms and worms, but cannot move into or through storm. Move up to 3 territories before the storm. Only forces in its current parent sector may enter by movement. It does not collect parent-territory spice and is separate for battles and occupancy.
findings.after: Ixian separate stronghold pointing at a sector of any non-stronghold territory, including the Polar Sink. Its occupants are protected from storm and worms. While Ixians occupy it, move it up to 3 territories before later storm movement is dialed or revealed; never into, out of or through storm. During its movement through a spice-bearing sector, immediately collect up to 2 spice per troop inside. Ixians may ship directly inside; other factions enter from the pointed territory by movement, with BG accompanying-shipment and Fremen worm-ride exceptions. It is separate for battles and counts as one stronghold.
findings.reason: Removed false sand-only/no-spice restrictions and unsupported same-sector-only entrance limit.

findings.before: Play as the weapon in your Battle Plan. Kills your opponent's leader. If a Shield is played in this battle, both leaders and all forces in the territory are killed, no spice is collected and both sides lose. You may keep this card if you win without an explosion.
findings.after: Play as the weapon in your Battle Plan. Kills your opponent's leader. If any Shield is played in this battle, destroy all spice and forces in the territory and kill both battle leaders. Neither side wins or collects leader spice. A traitor call overrides the explosion. You may keep this card if you win without an explosion.
findings.reason: Territory spice is destroyed, not merely leader spice withheld.
findings.source: GF9 core battle and card rules; collected FAQ6225364696

findings.before: Ecaz & Moritani Discovery module. The blow and Discovery token have separate locations. Follow the card text for each placement.
findings.after: Gain 7 spice from the Spice Bank, then remove this Discovery token from the game.
findings.reason: Replaced unrelated blow-placement boilerplate with actual token effect.

findings.before: Keep this token when revealed. On a subsequent turn, use it to move up to 3 territories for one movement action, then remove it from the game..
findings.after: Keep this token when revealed. On a subsequent turn, use it to move up to 3 territories for one movement action, then remove it from the game.
findings.reason: Removed doubled punctuation without changing effect.

findings.before: +1 free revival. +1 CHOAM Charity from the Bank. Once per faction on your Homeworld, force them to reveal their spice and either their weapons or defenses. Max 2 forces lost to Lasgun/Shield.
findings.after: +1 free revival. +1 CHOAM Charity from the Bank. When sharing a Homeworld with another faction, once per faction you may require it to reveal its spice and either its weapons or its defenses. Max 2 forces lost to Lasgun/Shield.
findings.reason: The collected card says same Homeworld as CHOAM, not only native Tupile.

findings.before: If at least one faction takes CHOAM Charity, gain 1 spice per Tech token you control, once this phase. No income if only Bene Gesserit alone triggers it. Place income on this token and collect at phase end. A battle winner takes one Tech token of their choice from a defeated holder. A single faction holding all three counts as one stronghold; allies cannot pool them. CHOAM gaining its faction Charity income alone does not trigger this token. Inflation never changes this income.
findings.after: If at least one faction takes CHOAM Charity, gain 1 spice from the Bank per Tech token you control, once this phase. No income if the only collectors are Bene Gesserit and/or CHOAM using their faction Charity advantages. Place income on this token and collect at phase end. A battle winner takes one Tech token of its choice from a defeated holder. One faction holding all three counts as one stronghold; allies cannot pool them. Inflation never changes this income.
findings.reason: Combined BG+CHOAM special incomes must not accidentally qualify when each alone does not.
findings.source: Ixians & Tleilaxu p5 and CHOAM & Richese p10

findings.before: After setup, stop one attempted use of a faction advantage, including an alliance advantage. In battle, play before plans are revealed. Or pay for any player's shipment at Guild rates, paid to the Bank. Or bid beyond your spice and buy a Treachery Card free, unless your hand is full or it is a Richese auction. Or use your once-per-game Special Karama Power. Cannot stop a special victory or Special Karama Power. Discard after use.
findings.after: After setup, stop one attempted use of a faction advantage, including an alliance advantage. In battle, play before plans are revealed. Or pay for any player's shipment at Guild rates, paid to the Bank. Or bid beyond your spice and buy a Treachery Card free, unless your hand is full or it is a Richese auction. findings.after: Bene Gesserit - Trigger the effect of any Ambassador that was not part of your supply, then remove this Bene Gesserit Ambassador from the game. Ecaz may trigger this immediately when a faction other than its ally or the matching faction enters with non-advisor forces. The effect interrupts the entering action. See Ecaz rules for the Ecaz alliance/Vidal choice.
findings.reason: Bene Gesserit Ambassador is used only once, rather than recycled with the other foreign Ambassadors.

findings.before: Richese - Pay 3 spice to the Bank for a Treachery Card. Ecaz may trigger this immediately when a faction other than its ally or the matching faction enters with non-advisor forces. The effect interrupts the entering action. See Ecaz rules for the Ecaz alliance/Vidal choice.
findings.after: Richese - If your hand is not full, pay 3 spice to the Bank to draw the top Treachery Card. Ecaz may trigger this immediately when a faction other than its ally or the matching faction enters with non-advisor forces. The effect interrupts the entering action. See Ecaz rules for the Ecaz alliance/Vidal choice.
findings.reason: Preserves the explicit hand-limit prerequisite.

findings.before: Ecaz - Gain Vidal if he is not in the Tanks, captured, or a ghola until used in a battle, or form an alliance with the visiting faction (if neither of you are allied); they may take control of Vidal instead. This token returns to your available supply. Ecaz may trigger this immediately when a faction other than its ally or the matching faction enters with non-advisor forces. findings.after: Ecaz - Gain Vidal if he is not in the Tanks, captured, or a ghola until used in a battle, or form an alliance with the visiting faction (if neither of you is allied and they agree); you may then give them control of Vidal for this turn. This token returns to your available supply. Ecaz may trigger this immediately when a faction other than its ally or the matching faction enters with non-advisor forces. The effect interrupts the entering action. See Ecaz rules for the Ecaz alliance/Vidal choice.
findings.reason: An alliance requires agreement; Vidal transfer is Ecaz choice and lasts this turn.

karama.assessment: Both shortened faces retain setup exclusion; one faction/alliance use; pre-reveal battle timing; any-player shipment to Bank at Guild rates; unlimited bid/free purchase with hand room; Richese-auction exclusion; Advanced-only once-per-game Special Karama; special-victory/Special-Karama immunity; discard after use.

tokenLabels.assessment: Face labels abbreviated; inspected all token faces and names. Full component names and effect text remain in data.

factionText.assessment: Ecaz short revival text retains only-Ecaz Vidal revival for5 and neutral set-aside. Special Karama title and nonbreaking-space adjustments change labels, not power text.

board.assessment: Existing adopted BoardMap output lacks territory names, sector numbers, printed spice points and tracks. This is recorded as an existing print-annotation limitation in the missing-features draft.

spiceCards.assessment: Short territory titles and sector captions retain maps and amounts. Discovery cards use the existing custom renderer to retain both distinct locations, sectors, quantities, token types, destruction and inspection rules without hidden text.
